lines.trans: I like your movie project very much.
It is an honour to act with you.
But I have a very strict condition.
Oh yes? Which one, dear Bernard?
I count all my steps.
No more than fifteen steps per scene!
Really? And for the dance scene?
A slow dance, very calm, I hope.
No, I chose the lindy hop!
The lindy hop? That is very fast!
Look, I am going to show you.
But what are you doing?
Dance with me, it is wonderful!
No, that is too many steps!

examples.text: Ça va? Oui, ça va bien.
examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

meanings.note: ça va? = how are you? / are you okay?

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.
examples.trans: There's a macaron on the table.

meanings.note: elle a quarante ans = she is forty

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

examples.trans: You know a lot of people.

meanings.en: beaucoup de = a lot of, many

meanings.note: une rue calme = a quiet street
before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.text: J'ai perdu un ami très cher.
examples.trans: I've lost a very dear friend.

meanings.note: before the noun: un ami très cher
after the noun or after être

examples.text: Des gens comptent sur ce film.
examples.trans: People are counting on this film.

meanings.en: compter sur = to count on, to rely on

meanings.note: la danse à la barre = pole dancing

examples.trans: I don't know how to dance.

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.

examples.trans: I hope to be like you.

meanings.note: pour faire quoi? = to do what?
faire du vélo = to ride a bike, to cycle

examples.text: Tu as fait quelque chose de formidable.
C'est un grand honneur pour vous!
examples.trans: It is a great honor for you!

examples.text: Il joue le frère de Guillaume.

meanings.note: jouer un rôle, jouer le frère de...
jouer au foot, jouer du piano
before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà

examples.text: Une danse lente, très calme, j'espère.
examples.trans: A slow dance, very calm, I hope.

examples.text: Le rythme du film est un peu lent.
examples.trans: The pace of the movie is a bit slow.

examples.text: Il doit y avoir une solution! — Laquelle?
examples.trans: There must be a solution! — Which one?

meanings.note: agrees in gender and number with the noun it replaces

examples.text: Non, j'ai choisi le lindy hop!
examples.trans: No, I chose the lindy hop!

examples.text: Elle apprend à danser le lindy hop.
examples.trans: She is learning to dance the lindy hop.

examples.text: Je veux, mais je ne peux pas.
examples.trans: I want to, but I can't.

meanings.note: tag at the end of a question

examples.text: Par exemple, le contrat de Canet.

meanings.en: pas du tout: not at all

meanings.note: invariable in plural: un pas, des pas
pronounced plys when it means 'more' at the end

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.
Tu as des projets ce soir?
Qu'est-ce que tu fais à Paris?
examples.trans: What are you doing in Paris?

meanings.note: starts a question: qu'est-ce que tu fais? = what are you doing?
au plus rapide = to the quickest one
une scène d'amour = a love scene

examples.text: Ça ne va pas du tout.

meanings.note: oui à tout = yes to everything
plural tous (pronounced 'tous' with s): merci à tous
before a noun: tout le monde = everyone

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

meanings.note: je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
